correctionAppended_2026-08-25.correction: Qdrant sparse vectors are (index, value) pairs with unsigned 32-bit indices; large, irregular indices are legal output of hashing, an explicit vocabulary mapping, a neural sparse encoder, or any other external scheme. Qdrant itself does not persist or expose a human-readable vocabulary just because a vector is sparse. modifier: 'idf' only tells Qdrant to apply shard-level inverse-document-frequency statistics to sparse query dimensions at query time -- it says nothing about how the sparse indices/values were produced. Therefore: 'idf modifier present' + 'irregular large indices' + 'no writer/vocabulary artifact found in this repo' is strong evidence of an OPAQUE EXTERNAL ENCODER of unknown mechanism, not specific proof of a hashing vectorizer.
